sentence_stem: Not only did the team finish the project early,
correct_completion: but they also exceeded every target set by the client.
full_sentence: Not only did the team finish the project early, but they also exceeded every target set by the client.
acceptable_variants: but they also reduced the costs considerably.
but they also earned the client's sincere praise.

options.why_wrong: 'Not only' needs a parallel, additive second element, and 'so' introduces a result that does not add a second achievement.

options.text: but they also exceeded every target set by the client.

options.why_wrong: This gives a background detail, but the structure 'not only... but also' needs a second positive achievement to add emphasis.
'Although' introduces a concession, which conflicts with the additive emphasis that 'not only' sets up.

grammar_focus: Correlative emphasis with 'not only... but also' and subject-auxiliary inversion
explanation: After 'not only', the sentence needs a second element of the same kind, introduced by 'but also', to build emphasis. Ukrainian speakers often treat the first clause as a simple statement and forget the parallel second clause, so the 'but also' part has to match the first clause in form and in importance.
translation: Команда не лише завершила проєкт раніше терміну, а й перевиконала всі цілі, встановлені замовником.
